name: Sts. Cyril and Methodius
bio:
Cyril and Methodius were brothers born in Thessalonica in the ninth century, sons of a Byzantine official. Both became scholars and monks; Cyril was known as Constantine the Philosopher before taking the name Cyril late in life. In 862 they were sent by the Byzantine emperor to evangelize the Slavic peoples of Moravia at the request of Prince Rastislav.

To preach in the language of the people, Cyril devised the Glagolitic alphabet, the ancestor of Cyrillic, and with Methodius translated the Gospels, the psalter, and the liturgy into Old Church Slavonic. Their work met fierce opposition from Frankish clergy who insisted on Latin, and they traveled to Rome to defend the Slavic liturgy, where Pope Adrian II approved it.

Cyril died in Rome in 869; Methodius continued as archbishop of Moravia until his death in 885. They are honored as the Apostles of the Slavs and patrons of missionaries and of Europe.

prayer.text: O God, who through Cyril and Methodius gave the Slavic peoples the Gospel in their own tongue, grant through their intercession that missionaries and the peoples of Europe may see the faith take root in every language and culture. We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.
